question: Nearly five years after the Taliban returned to Afghanistan with the help of the EU and its allies (i.e. the US), the EU has invited Taliban officials to Brussels for meetings. The purpose of the meeting is to discuss the deportation/‘return’ of Afghan migrants who are forbidden to stay in the EU.

The resolution on Afghanistan adopted by the European Parliament in plenary, not only condones the meeting but says nothing about the plan to deport Afghans from the EU and deliver them to the Taliban. In the same context, a few days ago, the EU announced the resumption of the full implementation of the cooperation agreement between the EU and AlSharaa jihadist Syria. In view of the above: 1.

Why is the Commission issuing invitations to representatives of the leadership of the obscurantist Taliban movement and maintaining corresponding relations with Syrian jihadists, whitewashing and financing them to carry out atrocities against the people of Afghanistan and Syria?

What is the Commission’s position on the fact that, by promoting deportations, the EU is prioritising relations and contacts with jihadist gangs such as those in Afghanistan and Syria, which carry out crimes and atrocities against the people of the two countries with a view to terrorising them, while in its Member States they persecute the Palestinian people with unfounded accusations of ‘terrorism’ as they resist Israeli occupation, along with trade unionists who express their solidarity with the people of Palestine?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.8.2026) The Commission was asked by 20 Member States and Schengen associated countries in a letter signed by their Ministers in October 2025, to coordinate contacts on returns with the de facto authorities, to ensure a coherent European approach. Their focus is on the return of persons posing a threat to public order or national security.
Returns to Afghanistan need to be addressed in a comprehensive and coordinated manner, bearing in mind the challenges arising from the acute humanitarian and human rights situation in Afghanistan.

The Commission and Sweden, on behalf of interested Member States, co-chaired a technical-level meeting with representatives of the de facto authorities of Afghanistan responsible for return and readmission, following technical-level discussions in Kabul, in January 2026. The technicallevel meeting aimed to give Member States the opportunity to address practical aspects of the readmission process.
15 Member States participated in the meeting. Operational engagement with the de facto authorities is in line with the Council conclusions of 15 September 20211 and 20 March 20232.

It does not constitute nor imply recognition, which remains conditioned upon progress on the EU’s established benchmarks, especially counterterrorism, inclusive governance and human rights, with particular concern for the rights of women and girls. The EU has strongly condemned the systemic violation of human rights.

The Commission acts in full respect of the Council conclusions and of its international obligations and will continue its unwavering support to all persons concerned by those violations of human rights. The first high-level political dialogue between the EU and Syria was held in Brussels on 11 May 2026.

The dialogue was an opportunity to discuss issues of strategic interest for Syria and the EU, including on migration. The work continues with the authorities and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to ensure that the conditions are conducive to safe, dignified and sustainable returns to Syria.

The EU is stepping up its work with the Syrian authorities and relevant partners to develop a comprehensive approach to migration and displacement. This means strengthening institutional capacities to address asylum and migration, including returns, and contributing to solutions for internally displaced populations.
